1	# Spec: Ops Sessions Page — Decisions
2	
3	> Pre-committed decisions captured 2026-05-14.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Decision matrix
8	
9	| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| Data source | `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-canonical>*/*.jsonl` (prefix glob to catch worktree-encoded keys; see Project-key resolution below) | Canonical Claude Code session location; no parallel store to maintain. Project-keyed encoding is `path.replace('/', '-')`. |
12	| Time window | **Last 3 days** | Patrick's call. "I don't want to maintain dated and useless data." Older sessions stay on disk but aren't surfaced. |
13	| Project scope | **Current project only** | Patrick's call. Cross-project resume is a power-user feature; current-project handles the 80% case. |
14	| Starter-prompt generation | **Haiku-summarized** (`claude-haiku-4-5`) | Patrick's call. Sharper than heuristic. ~$0.001/session × N=20 cap = ~$0.02/uncached load. |
15	| Heuristic fallback | First user prompt + last assistant turn, both truncated to ~200 chars | Used when LLM gate is off (`ATTUNE_OPS_SESSIONS_LLM=0`) OR Haiku call errors out. |
16	| Cache key | `(jsonl_filename, mtime, sha256_of_last_4kb)` | Hashes the JSONL tail — which actually changes as the session grows — rather than the byte-identical opening block. Single seek + read. See Cache-key collision below. |
17	| Cache location | `<attune_home>/ops/session_summaries/<session-id>.json` | Keeps session-specific data under `attune_home`, separate from `~/.claude/projects/` which we don't write to. |
18	| Cache TTL | None (mtime-bound) | A file that hasn't changed since last summary doesn't need re-summarizing. |
19	| List cap | **N=20 most-recent sessions** | Bounds Haiku spend per page load (~$0.02 worst case). Older sessions stay on disk for `cat`, not surfaced in the list. The Resume-most-recent card is unaffected and reads independently. See Budget-cap math below. |
20	| Budget cap per page load | `$0.05` | Hard cap; with N=20 it almost never fires in practice. Sessions beyond the cap render heuristic-only with a "summary unavailable — over budget" marker. Configurable via `[tool.attune-ops.sessions] budget_cap_usd`. |
21	| Listing route | `GET /sessions` (page) + `GET /api/sessions` (JSON) | Mirrors `/specs` + `/api/specs` and `/workflows` + `/api/runs/...`. |
22	| Listing JSON shape | `{sessions: [{id, started_at, last_activity, duration_seconds, message_count, starter_prompt, source}]}` where `source` ∈ `{"heuristic", "haiku", "cached"}` | Lets the UI show a "summarized by Haiku · cached" badge for transparency. |
23	| Expand-on-click body | Server-side render the first user message; full transcript stays at the JSONL file on disk (no in-page transcript viewer) | Keeps the page light. Users who want the full transcript can `cat` the JSONL. |
24	| Empty state | "No sessions in the last 3 days for this project. Older sessions are at `<path>`." | Tells the user where the data lives instead of pretending it doesn't. |
25	| Failure mode for unreadable JSONL | Skip with WARN log, don't surface as broken row | An unreadable file is a Claude Code internal issue, not something the user can fix from the dashboard. |
26	| "Resume most recent" card | **Yes — current-worktree first, canonical fallback** | Most-recent session from the dashboard's *own* encoded key (matches "where you are right now"). If none in last 3 days under the current key, fall back to the canonical project root's key. Dedupes against the list below. See Resume-card scope below. |
27	| Compare mode | `GET /sessions?compare=1` — renders heuristic + Haiku columns side-by-side for one request | Dev tool, no UI affordance. Pre-launch eyeball check that Haiku spend is buying actual quality. ~30 LOC + template tweak. |
28	| Calibration harness | Committed redacted JSONL fixtures + runner emitting `tokens / cost / quality` snapshot | Lands in S3 alongside the Haiku integration. Regression signal in CI for Haiku prompt edits. See Calibration as fixture below. |
29	| Live-session detection sources | (1) **`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var — verified present 2026-05-15**; (2) mtime within last 5 min on a session JSONL as a fallback | The pointer-file (`~/.claude/__last_session`) hypothesis was disproved during design probe — file does not exist. Env var name corrected from `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` to `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`. |
30	| Live-session card behavior | "You're currently in this session" label, suppress the duplicate row in the list below | Avoids surfacing a "resume" prompt for a session that doesn't need resuming. |
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Resolved design questions
35	
36	> All four open questions resolved 2026-05-15.
37	
38	### 1. Project-key resolution — read multiple keys (prefix-globbed)
39	
40	**Decision: read multiple encoded keys**, not canonicalize down
41	to one.
42	
43	**Why.** Empirical scan of `~/.claude/projects/` on 2026-05-15
44	showed the worktree-development setup produces a key per
45	worktree, not per logical project. For attune-ai specifically:
46	
47	- Canonical `-Users-patrickroebuck-attune-ai`: 44 sessions
48	- 47 distinct worktree-encoded keys
49	  (`-Users-patrickroebuck-attune-ai--claude-worktrees-<slug>`):
50	  57 sessions
51	- **93 sessions in the last 3 days across all keys**
52	
53	Canonical-only lookup would miss the majority of recent
54	sessions in this dev pattern. Patrick's instinct was right;
55	the data forced the resolution.
56	
57	**Implementation.**
58	
59	- Compute encoded prefix from
60	  `Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve()` →
61	  `str.replace('/', '-')`.
62	- Glob `~/.claude/projects/<encoded>*` for matching dirs.
63	- Accept a dir iff its name equals `<encoded>` exactly, OR
64	  starts with `<encoded>-` (the `-` separator guards against
65	  sibling-project false matches like `attune-ai-something`).
66	- Read all `*.jsonl` from matched dirs.
67	- Dedup sessions by session-id (the JSONL filename's stem) —
68	  if a session somehow appears under multiple keys, the
69	  newest-mtime copy wins; log a WARN.
70	
71	### 2. Haiku prompt template — calibration-driven
72	
73	**Decision: design through a 5–10 session calibration pass
74	before defaulting.**
75	
76	**Target output shape.** A starter prompt that:
77	
78	1. Names what was being worked on (1 short sentence).
79	2. Lists any open threads (bullets, 0–3 items).
80	3. Suggests a 1-sentence resume prompt the user can paste.
81	
82	**Calibration plan.** Pick 5–10 real sessions of varying
83	length from `~/.claude/projects/-Users-patrickroebuck-attune-ai*`;
84	run the candidate prompt against each; manually score the
85	output against the target shape. Iterate the template until
86	the median output is ship-worthy. The finalized prompt text
87	lands in the calibration record below.
88	
89	### 3. Active prompt-redaction — yes, explicit pass
90	
91	**Decision: add a redaction pass before sending to Haiku.**
92	
93	**Why.** Relying on the model to "naturally summarize away"
94	sensitive content is non-deterministic — one session out of
95	fifty leaks a token verbatim into a cached summary and that's
96	a real incident. An explicit pass is cheap and bounded.
97	
98	**Patterns to redact (initial set; extend as we learn).**
99	
100	- API key shapes:
101	  `sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`, `sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}`,
102	  `ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}`, `gho_…`, `ghu_…`, `xoxb-…`,
103	  `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`, generic `[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}` tokens
104	  preceded by `key|token|secret|password` within 5 chars.
105	- Bearer-style headers: `Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]+`.
106	- Absolute paths under `~` or `/Users/<name>/` — replace
107	  with `<user-home>` or `<...>` (paths inside the project
108	  root are kept; they're useful context).
109	- IP addresses (RFC 1918 + public).
110	- Email addresses outside a small allowlist (Patrick's own
111	  emails per CLAUDE.md are fine; redact the rest).
112	
113	**Order.** Redact first, then send to Haiku, then cache the
114	already-redacted summary. The cache never holds a sensitive
115	prompt; subsequent reads inherit the redaction for free.
116	
117	### 4. Live-session detection — env var + mtime fallback
118	
119	**Decision: 2-layer detection, env var primary.**
120	
121	**Empirical findings (probed inside a Claude Code session
122	2026-05-15):**
123	
124	- `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var **is present**
125	  (e.g. `accc710d-5f39-46bb-bf8b-06d779a03291`). Note: the
126	  spec draft had this as `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` — wrong name.
127	  Actual variable has the `CODE_` infix. Same value the
128	  JSONL file is named after.
129	- `~/.claude/__last_session` (and obvious variants
130	  `last_session`, `session`) **does not exist** on disk.
131	  Was a guess; dropping from the design.
132	- `~/.claude/sessions/` directory does exist but appears
133	  unrelated to per-project session detection — out of scope
134	  for this design.
135	
136	**Implementation.**
137	
138	1. Read `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` from the dashboard's process
139	   env. If present, that's the live session.
140	2. Fallback: any `.jsonl` whose mtime is within the last 5
141	   minutes is considered "potentially live." If exactly one
142	   matches, treat as live. If multiple, no live indicator
143	   (don't guess).
144	
145	The dashboard process inherits the env from whatever shell
146	launched it, which means: when launched from inside a Claude
147	Code session, the dashboard correctly detects "that
148	session." When launched from a plain shell, only the mtime
149	fallback fires.
150	
151	---
152	
153	## Pre-S3 design tightening
154	
155	> Five additional resolutions captured 2026-05-15 after a
156	> review pass. Each tightens a decision that the original
157	> matrix made on incomplete information.
158	
159	### 5. Budget-cap math — list capped at N=20
160	
161	**Problem.** The original $0.05/load cap was sized for
162	"~10 sessions in a 3-day window." The multi-key probe found
163	**93 sessions** in the same window across all encoded keys
164	— ~9× the original estimate. At ~$0.001/session that's
165	~$0.09 per uncached load: already 1.8× over the cap before
166	caching takes effect.
167	
168	**Decision.** Cap the surfaced list at **N=20 most-recent
169	sessions** (sorted by `last_activity` desc). Worst-case
170	uncached spend: 20 × $0.001 = $0.02 — well under the $0.05
171	cap, with headroom for prompt growth or input-size variance.
172

## Resolved design questions

> All four open questions resolved 2026-05-15.

### 1. Project-key resolution — read multiple keys (prefix-globbed)

**Decision: read multiple encoded keys**, not canonicalize down
to one.

**Why.** Empirical scan of `~/.claude/projects/` on 2026-05-15
showed the worktree-development setup produces a key per
worktree, not per logical project. For attune-ai specifically:

- Canonical `-Users-patrickroebuck-attune-ai`: 44 sessions
- 47 distinct worktree-encoded keys
  (`-Users-patrickroebuck-attune-ai--claude-worktrees-<slug>`):
  57 sessions
- **93 sessions in the last 3 days across all keys**

Canonical-only lookup would miss the majority of recent
sessions in this dev pattern. Patrick's instinct was right;
the data forced the resolution.

**Implementation.**

- Compute encoded prefix from
  `Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve()` →
  `str.replace('/', '-')`.
- Glob `~/.claude/projects/<encoded>*` for matching dirs.
- Accept a dir iff its name equals `<encoded>` exactly, OR
  starts with `<encoded>-` (the `-` separator guards against
  sibling-project false matches like `attune-ai-something`).
- Read all `*.jsonl` from matched dirs.
- Dedup sessions by session-id (the JSONL filename's stem) —
  if a session somehow appears under multiple keys, the
  newest-mtime copy wins; log a WARN.

### 2. Haiku prompt template — calibration-driven

**Decision: design through a 5–10 session calibration pass
before defaulting.**

**Target output shape.** A starter prompt that:

1. Names what was being worked on (1 short sentence).
2. Lists any open threads (bullets, 0–3 items).
3. Suggests a 1-sentence resume prompt the user can paste.

**Calibration plan.** Pick 5–10 real sessions of varying
length from `~/.claude/projects/-Users-patrickroebuck-attune-ai*`;
run the candidate prompt against each; manually score the
output against the target shape. Iterate the template until
the median output is ship-worthy. The finalized prompt text
lands in the calibration record below.

### 3. Active prompt-redaction — yes, explicit pass

**Decision: add a redaction pass before sending to Haiku.**

**Why.** Relying on the model to "naturally summarize away"
sensitive content is non-deterministic — one session out of
fifty leaks a token verbatim into a cached summary and that's
a real incident. An explicit pass is cheap and bounded.

**Patterns to redact (initial set; extend as we learn).**

- API key shapes:
  `sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`, `sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}`,
  `ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}`, `gho_…`, `ghu_…`, `xoxb-…`,
  `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`, generic `[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}` tokens
  preceded by `key|token|secret|password` within 5 chars.
- Bearer-style headers: `Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]+`.
- Absolute paths under `~` or `/Users/<name>/` — replace
  with `<user-home>` or `<...>` (paths inside the project
  root are kept; they're useful context).
- IP addresses (RFC 1918 + public).
- Email addresses outside a small allowlist (Patrick's own
  emails per CLAUDE.md are fine; redact the rest).

**Order.** Redact first, then send to Haiku, then cache the
already-redacted summary. The cache never holds a sensitive
prompt; subsequent reads inherit the redaction for free.

**Decision: 2-layer detection, env var primary.**

**Empirical findings (probed inside a Claude Code session
2026-05-15):**

- `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var **is present**
  (e.g. `accc710d-5f39-46bb-bf8b-06d779a03291`). Note: the
  spec draft had this as `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` — wrong name.
  Actual variable has the `CODE_` infix. Same value the
  JSONL file is named after.
- `~/.claude/__last_session` (and obvious variants
  `last_session`, `session`) **does not exist** on disk.
  Was a guess; dropping from the design.
- `~/.claude/sessions/` directory does exist but appears
  unrelated to per-project session detection — out of scope
  for this design.

**Implementation.**

1. Read `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` from the dashboard's process
   env. If present, that's the live session.
2. Fallback: any `.jsonl` whose mtime is within the last 5
   minutes is considered "potentially live." If exactly one
   matches, treat as live. If multiple, no live indicator
   (don't guess).

The dashboard process inherits the env from whatever shell
launched it, which means: when launched from inside a Claude
Code session, the dashboard correctly detects "that
session." When launched from a plain shell, only the mtime
fallback fires.

# Spec: Ops Dashboard — Sessions Page

> Add a `/sessions` page to the ops dashboard surfacing the last 3
> days of Claude Code sessions for the **current project**, each with
> a Haiku-summarized starter-prompt for resuming.

---

## Phase 1: Requirements

**Status**: draft

### Problem statement

The 2026-05-14 QA punch list flagged that `/sessions` returns 404 —
no template exists (P1-4). Patrick confirmed: keep Sessions, drop
Memory, narrow scope. The use case: refreshing memory on what was
worked on across recent Claude Code sessions, so a new session can
start with context rather than from scratch.

Existing context-recovery surface today: re-reading transcripts
manually from `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-path>/`. Each transcript
is a `.jsonl` file with line-delimited messages — useful but
high-friction. A dashboard surface that lists recent sessions with
short summaries and copy-pasteable starter prompts is the UX win.

### Scope

**In scope:**

- New page `/sessions` in the ops dashboard.
- Data source: `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-current-project>/*.jsonl`
  where the encoding is the current-project absolute path with `/`
  replaced by `-`. The dashboard's `cfg.project_root` provides the
  unencoded path.
- Time window: only sessions with mtime within the last **3 days**.
- Scope: current project only (no cross-project listing).
- Per-session display (table or card layout):
  - Session id (short, ~8 chars of the UUID)
  - Started timestamp (relative + absolute on hover, matching the
    Updated column pattern on Specs)
  - Duration (last message timestamp minus first)
  - Message count
  - **Starter prompt** — Haiku-summarized one-paragraph summary +
    a suggested first prompt for resuming the session
- Click → expand to show the first user message in full (truncated
  to ~500 chars) plus a "Copy starter prompt to clipboard" button.
- A "Sessions older than 3 days are hidden" footer note so users
  understand the filter (not actively pruned from disk — Claude
  Code owns that).
- **"Resume most recent" prominent action.** The single newest
  session (by mtime) for the current project gets a dedicated
  card at the top of the page — separate from the rest-of-list
  treatment. Includes:
  - The Haiku-summarized starter prompt rendered in full (not
    truncated)
  - A one-click "Copy starter prompt" button
  - A "Resume in a new Claude Code session" hint that walks
    the user through pasting the prompt into a fresh session
  - When the in-progress Claude Code session ID is detectable
    (via `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` env var, `~/.claude/__last_session`
    pointer, or equivalent — investigate during design phase),
    the card flips to show "You're currently in this session"
    with no starter-prompt needed; suppresses the duplicate row
    further down the list.

**Out of scope:**

- Cross-project session listing
- Filtering / search beyond the time-window default
- Editing sessions
- Resuming a session in-process (just copies a starter prompt)
- Memory page (explicitly dropped by Patrick, 2026-05-14)

### Acceptance criteria

1. Navigating to `/sessions` returns HTTP 200 with a list of the
   project's sessions from the last 3 days, sorted newest first.
2. Each session row shows id, started time, duration, message
   count, and a Haiku-generated starter prompt.
3. Sessions older than 3 days are not shown.
3a. The newest session renders in the "Resume most recent" card
   at the top, with its full Haiku-summarized starter prompt and
   a copy-to-clipboard button. The same session does NOT also
   appear in the list below.
3b. When the dashboard is launched from inside a Claude Code
   session and that session's id can be resolved against the
   project's session directory, the "Resume most recent" card
   labels itself "You're currently in this session" instead of
   surfacing a resume prompt.
4. Sessions with empty / unreadable JSONL files are skipped
   (logged at WARN, not surfaced as broken rows).
5. The Haiku summarization is gated by `ATTUNE_OPS_SESSIONS_LLM=1`
   or an equivalent opt-in; with the gate off, a heuristic summary
   (first user prompt + last assistant turn truncated) is used.
6. Session summaries are cached on disk under
   `<attune_home>/ops/session_summaries/<session-id>.json` keyed
   by the JSONL file's mtime+sha256, so the same session isn't
   re-summarized on every page load.
7. Total cost per full page load (assuming cache miss on every
   session shown) stays below `$0.05` — bounded by the 3-day
   window and Haiku pricing.

### Non-goals / explicitly deferred

- **Pruning Claude Code's sessions directory.** Not our job.
- **Live in-progress session detection.** Could be a Phase 2
  follow-up — the currently-running Claude Code instance has a
  PID and could be cross-referenced, but the read-only Sessions
  page can punt.
- **Cross-machine session sync.** Out of scope — sessions live
  on the local machine only.

### Risks

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Encoded-path heuristic doesn't always match Claude Code's logic | Med | Read `~/.claude/projects/` directly, find the dir whose name is `cfg.project_root` with `/` → `-`; fall back to any single dir if there's only one (single-project user) |
| JSONL parsing is slow for many large sessions | Low | Only read the first line (start timestamp + first user message) and the file's mtime — no full parse for the listing view. Full parse only on expand. |
| Haiku summarization adds visible cost | Med | Cache aggressively; opt-in flag for first release; budget cap per page load |
| Summary quality varies | Low | Phase 1 ships heuristic + Haiku; if Haiku underperforms, fall back |

39	class PathArgSpec:
40	    """How a workflow accepts a scope path on the CLI.

75	PATH_ARG_REGISTRY: dict[str, PathArgSpec] = {

112	    """One feature from ``.help/features.yaml`` for the scope picker.
113	
114	    ``path`` is a single representative repo-relative path derived from
115	    the feature's ``files`` list: prefer a directory glob (entry ending
116	    in ``/**``, stripped of the suffix); otherwise the first non-glob
117	    entry. ``None`` when the feature has no addressable scope (empty
118	    ``files`` or only mid-name globs like ``code_review_*.py``).
119	    """

121	    name: str
122	    description: str
123	    path: str | None
124	    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()

127	# Per-yaml-file mtime cache: {abs_path: (mtime_ns, features_in_yaml_order)}.
128	# Stores features in YAML insertion order; ``list_features()`` returns a
129	# sorted copy, ``most_recent_feature()`` reads the cache directly.
130	_FEATURES_CACHE: dict[str, tuple[int, list[Feature]]] = {}
131	
132	
133	def _derive_feature_path(files: list[str]) -> str | None:
134	    """Pick a representative scope path from a feature's files list.
135	
136	    Preference order:
137	      1. First entry ending in ``/**`` (a directory scope) — strip the suffix.
138	      2. First entry with no glob metacharacters (a single file).
139	      3. ``None`` otherwise.
140	    """
141	    for entry in files:
142	        if entry.endswith("/**"):
143	            return entry[: -len("/**")]
144	    for entry in files:
145	        if "*" not in entry and "?" not in entry and "[" not in entry:
146	            return entry
147	    return None
148	
149	
150	def _features_in_yaml_order(project_root: Path | str) -> list[Feature]:
151	    """Parse ``features.yaml`` and return features in YAML insertion order.
152	
153	    Internal helper. Callers wanting alphabetical display use
154	    :func:`list_features`; callers wanting the most-recently-added feature
155	    use :func:`most_recent_feature`. Both share this cached parse.
156	
157	    Returns ``[]`` on missing file, unreadable file, or malformed YAML.
158	    Cached by mtime so repeated calls within one server run skip the parse.
159	    """
160	    root = Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve()
161	    yaml_path = root / ".help" / "features.yaml"
162	    if not yaml_path.is_file():
163	        return []
164	
165	    try:
166	        mtime_ns = yaml_path.stat().st_mtime_ns
167	    except OSError:
168	        return []
169	
170	    cache_key = str(yaml_path)
171	    cached = _FEATURES_CACHE.get(cache_key)
172	    if cached is not None and cached[0] == mtime_ns:
173	        return cached[1]
174	
175	    try:
176	        import yaml as _yaml
177	    except ImportError:
178	        return []
179	    try:
180	        text = yaml_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
181	        raw = _yaml.safe_load(text)
182	    except (OSError, _yaml.YAMLError):
183	        return []
184	
185	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
186	        return []
187	    raw_features = raw.get("features")
188	    if not isinstance(raw_features, dict):
189	        return []
190	
191	    out: list[Feature] = []
192	    for name, spec in raw_features.items():
193	        if not isinstance(spec, dict):

195	        files_raw = spec.get("files") or []
196	        files = (
197	            [str(f) for f in files_raw if isinstance(f, str)] if isinstance(files_raw, list) else []

199	        tags_raw = spec.get("tags") or []

203	            else ()
204	        )

285	def derive_project_name(project_root: Path | str) -> str:
286	    """Return a human-readable project name for the dashboard header.
287	
288	    Reads the ``[project]`` table's ``name`` field from
289	    ``<project_root>/pyproject.toml`` when present; falls back to the
290	    directory basename otherwise. The fallback gives sensible output
291	    for projects without a ``pyproject.toml`` (Node.js, plain
292	    directories) while the pyproject path means worktree-launched
293	    dashboards display the package name (e.g. ``attune-ai``) instead
294	    of the worktree slug (e.g. ``reverent-brown-937823``).
295	
296	    Defensive failure modes — none of these surface to the user; the
297	    dashboard just renders the basename:
298	
299	    - Missing ``pyproject.toml`` → basename.
300	    - Unreadable file (perm error, OSError) → basename.
301	    - Malformed TOML → basename.
302	    - ``[project]`` table missing or ``name`` field missing → basename.
303	    - Empty ``name`` value → basename (don't render blank header).
304	
305	    No-pyproject fallback chain isn't extended to ancestor
306	    directories: the dashboard's ``--project-root`` is supposed to
307	    BE the project root. Walking up could surface a parent
308	    workspace's name (e.g. ``Users``) which is worse than the
309	    worktree slug.
310	    """
311	    root = Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve()
312	    pyproject = root / "pyproject.toml"
313	    if pyproject.is_file():
314	        try:
315	            text = pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
316	        except OSError:
317	            return root.name
318	        # Python 3.11+ ships tomllib; fall back to the stdlib parser.
319	        try:
320	            import tomllib
321	        except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover — Python < 3.11
322	            try:
323	                import tomli as tomllib  # type: ignore[no-redef]
324	            except ImportError:
325	                return root.name
326	        try:
327	            parsed = tomllib.loads(text)
328	        except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
329	            return root.name
330	        project_table = parsed.get("project")
331	        if isinstance(project_table, dict):
332	            name = project_table.get("name")
333	            if isinstance(name, str) and name.strip():
334	                return name.strip()
335	    return root.name

364	def _encoded_project_path(project_root: Path | str) -> str:
365	    """Claude Code encodes its project subdir as ``path.replace('/', '-')``.
366	
367	    Resolves to absolute first so a relative ``project_root`` arg
368	    still matches the on-disk encoding. Returns the encoded
369	    basename only — the caller prepends ``~/.claude/projects/``.
370	
371	    Three characters are mapped to ``-`` so the resulting string is
372	    safe to concatenate as a single path segment on every platform:
373	
374	    - ``/`` — POSIX path separator (matches Claude Code's documented
375	      encoding).
376	    - ``\\`` — Windows path separator. ``Path.resolve()`` produces
377	      backslashes on Windows.
378	    - ``:`` — Windows drive-letter delimiter (``D:``). Without
379	      this, the encoded string contains a literal ``D:`` prefix that
380	      pathlib treats as a drive specifier on subsequent
381	      ``Path / encoded`` concatenation, silently discarding the
382	      ``~/.claude/projects/`` prefix and rooting the result at the
383	      bogus drive.
384	
385	    POSIX paths never contain backslash or colon, so the two
386	    Windows-only replacements are no-ops there.
387	    """
388	    resolved = str(Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve())
389	    return resolved.replace("/", "-").replace("\\", "-").replace(":", "-")

403	def _heuristic_starter_prompt(content: str, *, char_limit: int = 200) -> str:
404	    """Truncate a user's first-prompt content to ~``char_limit`` chars.
405	
406	    Spec calls for first user prompt + last assistant turn, both
407	    truncated. The Claude Code JSONL we observed only carries the
408	    user-prompt side via queue-operation enqueue events; there's no
409	    assistant-turn signal in this event log. S2 ships with the
410	    user-prompt-only heuristic; S3's Haiku path produces the
411	    fuller summary independently of this code path.
412	
413	    Truncation strategy: cut at a word boundary if one falls within
414	    ``char_limit - 20`` of the limit so we don't slice mid-word.
415	    Ellipsis appended when truncated.
416	    """
417	    s = (content or "").strip().replace("\n", " ")
418	    # Collapse runs of whitespace so the preview doesn't have gaps.
419	    s = " ".join(s.split())
420	    if len(s) <= char_limit:
421	        return s
422	    cut = s[:char_limit]
423	    last_space = cut.rfind(" ")
424	    if last_space > char_limit - 20:
425	        cut = cut[:last_space]
426	    return cut.rstrip() + "…"

429	def _parse_session(jsonl_path: Path) -> Session | None:
430	    """Build a :class:`Session` from one JSONL file. Returns None on
431	    unreadable file (callers skip rather than crash the listing).
432	
433	    Robust per-line: a malformed JSON line is skipped, not fatal.
434	    A file with zero parseable lines yields a Session with empty
435	    timestamps and a "(empty session)" starter prompt — the
436	    template can render the row OR the caller can filter; we
437	    surface rather than hide.
438	    """
439	    session_id = jsonl_path.stem
440	    first_ts: str | None = None
441	    last_ts: str | None = None
442	    prompt_count = 0
443	    starter_prompt = ""
444	    try:
445	        with jsonl_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
446	            for raw in fh:
447	                line = raw.strip()
448	                if not line:
449	                    continue
450	                try:
451	                    event = json.loads(line)
452	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
453	                    continue
454	                if not isinstance(event, dict):
455	                    continue
456	                ts = event.get("timestamp")
457	                if isinstance(ts, str) and ts:
458	                    if first_ts is None:
459	                        first_ts = ts
460	                    last_ts = ts
461	                content = event.get("content")
462	                if isinstance(content, str) and content:
463	                    prompt_count += 1
464	                    if not starter_prompt:
465	                        starter_prompt = _heuristic_starter_prompt(content)
466	    except OSError:
467	        return None
468	    duration = _duration_seconds(first_ts, last_ts)
469	    return Session(
470	        id=session_id,
471	        started_at=first_ts or "",
472	        last_activity=last_ts or first_ts or "",
473	        duration_seconds=duration,
474	        message_count=prompt_count,
475	        starter_prompt=starter_prompt or "(no prompt recorded)",
476	        source="heuristic",
477	    )

480	def _duration_seconds(first: str | None, last: str | None) -> float:
481	    """ISO 8601 strings → elapsed seconds; ``0.0`` if either is unparseable."""
482	    if not first or not last:
483	        return 0.0
484	    try:
485	        a = datetime.fromisoformat(first.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
486	        b = datetime.fromisoformat(last.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
487	    except ValueError:
488	        return 0.0
489	    return max((b - a).total_seconds(), 0.0)

492	def list_recent_sessions(
493	    project_root: Path | str,
494	    *,
495	    days: int = 3,
496	    now: datetime | None = None,
497	) -> list[Session]:
498	    """Return Session records for this project's last ``days`` of activity.
499	
500	    Reads ``~/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-root>/*.jsonl`` and
501	    filters to files whose mtime is within ``days`` of ``now``
502	    (default: current UTC time). Sorts most-recently-active first.
503	
504	    Returns ``[]`` for any failure mode that doesn't raise:
505	    - Sessions dir doesn't exist (user never ran Claude Code here)
506	    - Sessions dir exists but is empty
507	    - All JSONLs are older than the cutoff
508	    - All JSONLs are unreadable (perm, IO)
509	
510	    A single corrupt file is skipped with a WARN log; the rest of
511	    the listing still renders. The spec's failure-mode decision:
512	    "Skip with WARN log, don't surface as broken row — an unreadable
513	    file is a Claude Code internal issue, not something the user
514	    can fix from the dashboard."
515	    """
516	    # Local import: a module-level ``timedelta`` import was reverted by
517	    # the formatter (likely ruff isort considering it unused at the
518	    # module scope since only this function references it). Re-importing
519	    # locally is the pragmatic dodge — the cost is negligible because
520	    # ``from datetime import ...`` is cached after first use anyway.
521	    from datetime import timedelta
522	
523	    sessions_dir = claude_sessions_dir(project_root)
524	    if not sessions_dir.is_dir():
525	        return []
526	    if now is None:
527	        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
528	    cutoff = now - timedelta(days=days)
529	    out: list[Session] = []
530	    try:
531	        candidates = list(sessions_dir.glob("*.jsonl"))
532	    except OSError:
533	        return []
534	    for jsonl in candidates:
535	        try:
536	            mtime = datetime.fromtimestamp(jsonl.stat().st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc)
537	        except OSError:
538	            continue
539	        if mtime < cutoff:
540	            continue
541	        session = _parse_session(jsonl)
542	        if session is None:
543	            continue
544	        out.append(session)
545	    out.sort(key=lambda s: s.last_activity or "", reverse=True)
546	    return out

630	def read_telemetry_summary(config: Config, *, recent_days: int = 7) -> TelemetrySummary:
631	    """Aggregate ``usage.jsonl`` into a UI-friendly summary."""
632	    path = config.telemetry_path
633	    if not path.exists():
634	        return TelemetrySummary(0, 0.0, 0.0, [], [], None)
635	
636	    total_requests = 0
637	    total_cost = 0.0
638	    total_savings = 0.0
639	    by_workflow_count: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
640	    by_workflow_cost: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
641	    by_day_count: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
642	    by_day_cost: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
643	    last_event_at: str | None = None
644	
645	    try:
646	        with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
647	            for line in f:
648	                line = line.strip()
649	                if not line:
650	                    continue
651	                try:
652	                    event: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(line)
653	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
654	                    continue
655	
656	                cost = float(event.get("total_cost", event.get("cost", 0.0)) or 0.0)
657	                savings = float(event.get("savings", 0.0) or 0.0)
658	                workflow = str(event.get("workflow") or event.get("event_type") or "unknown")
659	                # ``usage.jsonl`` events use the ``ts`` key (v1.0 schema in
660	                # UsageTracker._format_entry); ``timestamp`` is kept as a
661	                # legacy fallback for any rotated archives that predate the
662	                # rename. Without this fallback every event silently misses
663	                # the by_day bucketing and Home's KPI tiles read zero.
664	                ts = str(event.get("ts") or event.get("timestamp") or "")
665	
666	                total_requests += 1
667	                total_cost += cost
668	                total_savings += savings
669	                by_workflow_count[workflow] += 1
670	                by_workflow_cost[workflow] += cost
671	
672	                day = _to_day(ts)
673	                if day:
674	                    by_day_count[day] += 1
675	                    by_day_cost[day] += cost
676	                if ts:
677	                    last_event_at = ts
678	    except OSError:
679	        return TelemetrySummary(0, 0.0, 0.0, [], [], None)
680	
681	    # Filter test fixtures, demo stubs, and removed workflows from the
682	    # top-list. The telemetry file accumulates entries from every
683	    # workflow that ever ran, so old test fixtures (e.g. those listed
684	    # in .claude/rules/attune/bug-patterns.md sync logs:
685	    # "test-tier-fallback", "new-sample-workflow1") pollute the top
686	    # spenders rollup and distort the "where did my money go?" signal.
687	    # The current registry is the source of truth — anything not in it
688	    # is either a removed workflow or a stub from local development.
689	    # (P2-8 in the 2026-05-14 QA punch list.)
690	    try:
691	        canonical_names = {w.name for w in list_workflows()}
692	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
693	        # INTENTIONAL: if the registry introspection fails, fall back
694	        # to showing everything rather than hiding all data.
695	        canonical_names = None
696	
697	    def _is_canonical(name: str) -> bool:
698	        if canonical_names is None:
699	            return True
700	        return name in canonical_names
701	
702	    filtered = [
703	        (k, by_workflow_count[k], round(by_workflow_cost[k], 4))
704	        for k in by_workflow_count
705	        if _is_canonical(k)
706	    ]
707	    by_workflow = sorted(filtered, key=lambda row: row[2], reverse=True)[:20]
708	
709	    today = date.today()
710	    cutoff = today.toordinal() - recent_days
711	    recent_days_data = sorted(
712	        (
713	            (day, by_day_count[day], round(by_day_cost[day], 4))
714	            for day in by_day_count
715	            if _ordinal(day) is not None and _ordinal(day) >= cutoff
716	        ),
717	        key=lambda row: row[0],
718	    )
719	
720	    return TelemetrySummary(
721	        total_requests=total_requests,
722	        total_cost=round(total_cost, 4),
723	        total_savings=round(total_savings, 4),
724	        by_workflow=by_workflow,
725	        by_day=recent_days_data,
726	        last_event_at=last_event_at,
727	    )

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Feature:
    """One feature from ``.help/features.yaml`` for the scope picker.

    ``path`` is a single representative repo-relative path derived from
    the feature's ``files`` list: prefer a directory glob (entry ending
    in ``/**``, stripped of the suffix); otherwise the first non-glob
    entry. ``None`` when the feature has no addressable scope (empty
    ``files`` or only mid-name globs like ``code_review_*.py``).
    """

    name: str
    description: str
    path: str | None
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()


# Per-yaml-file mtime cache: {abs_path: (mtime_ns, features_in_yaml_order)}.
# Stores features in YAML insertion order; ``list_features()`` returns a
# sorted copy, ``most_recent_feature()`` reads the cache directly.
_FEATURES_CACHE: dict[str, tuple[int, list[Feature]]] = {}


def _derive_feature_path(files: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Pick a representative scope path from a feature's files list.

    Preference order:
      1. First entry ending in ``/**`` (a directory scope) — strip the suffix.
      2. First entry with no glob metacharacters (a single file).
      3. ``None`` otherwise.
    """
    for entry in files:
        if entry.endswith("/**"):
            return entry[: -len("/**")]
    for entry in files:
        if "*" not in entry and "?" not in entry and "[" not in entry:
            return entry
    return None


def _features_in_yaml_order(project_root: Path | str) -> list[Feature]:
    """Parse ``features.yaml`` and return features in YAML insertion order.

    Internal helper. Callers wanting alphabetical display use
    :func:`list_features`; callers wanting the most-recently-added feature
    use :func:`most_recent_feature`. Both share this cached parse.

    Returns ``[]`` on missing file, unreadable file, or malformed YAML.
    Cached by mtime so repeated calls within one server run skip the parse.
    """
    root = Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve()
    yaml_path = root / ".help" / "features.yaml"
    if not yaml_path.is_file():
        return []

    try:
        mtime_ns = yaml_path.stat().st_mtime_ns
    except OSError:
        return []

    cache_key = str(yaml_path)
    cached = _FEATURES_CACHE.get(cache_key)
    if cached is not None and cached[0] == mtime_ns:
        return cached[1]

    try:
        import yaml as _yaml
    except ImportError:
        return []
    try:
        text = yaml_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        raw = _yaml.safe_load(text)
    except (OSError, _yaml.YAMLError):
        return []

    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return []
    raw_features = raw.get("features")
    if not isinstance(raw_features, dict):
        return []

    out: list[Feature] = []
    for name, spec in raw_features.items():
        if not isinstance(spec, dict):
            continue
        files_raw = spec.get("files") or []
        files = (
            [str(f) for f in files_raw if isinstance(f, str)] if isinstance(files_raw, list) else []
        )
        tags_raw = spec.get("tags") or []
        tags = (
            tuple(str(t) for t in tags_raw if isinstance(t, str))
            if isinstance(tags_raw, list)
            else ()
        )
        out.append(
            Feature(
                name=str(name),
                description=str(spec.get("description") or ""),
                path=_derive_feature_path(files),
                tags=tags,
            )
        )
    _FEATURES_CACHE[cache_key] = (mtime_ns, out)
    return out


def list_features(project_root: Path | str) -> list[Feature]:
    """Return features parsed from ``<project_root>/.help/features.yaml``.

    Returns ``[]`` on missing file, unreadable file, or malformed YAML.
    Result is sorted alphabetically by feature name (findability in the
    picker dropdown). Backed by a mtime-keyed cache shared with
    :func:`most_recent_feature`.
    """
    return sorted(_features_in_yaml_order(project_root), key=lambda f: f.name)


def first_feature(project_root: Path | str) -> Feature | None:
    """Return the alphabetically-first feature with a renderable scope.

    Used by the ops dashboard scope picker as the primary first-load
    fallback when ``localStorage`` has no saved scope. Predictable +
    stable: the same feature is returned regardless of YAML ordering
    changes, so the picker doesn't surprise the user by jumping around
    when features are reordered.

    Only features with a non-``None`` ``path`` are considered, since
    those are the only ones rendered as picker options. When no
    path-bearing feature exists, the dashboard falls through to the
    "All code" option (see :data:`ALL_CODE_PATH`). Returns ``None``
    if ``features.yaml`` is missing, empty, or has no path-bearing
    entries.
    """
    for feature in list_features(project_root):
        if feature.path:
            return feature
    return None


def workflow_default_scope(workflow_name: str, project_root: Path | str) -> str:
    """Return the default scope for one workflow on first paint.

    Auto-derives by exact-name match against ``features.yaml``: if a
    feature with the same name as the workflow exists and has a
    renderable ``path``, that path is the default. Otherwise returns
    ``""`` (project-wide), which is the safe fallback the picker
    template already renders as the first option.

    Used by the dashboard route to render a per-row
    ``data-scope-default`` attribute on each workflow row, so the JS
    can restore a workflow-appropriate scope on first load instead of
    defaulting every row to the alphabetically-first feature.

    Example match table for the attune-ai ``features.yaml``:

    - ``security-audit`` workflow → ``src/attune/security`` (matches
      the ``security-audit`` feature's ``files: [..., src/attune/
      security/**]`` entry).
    - ``release-prep`` workflow → ``""`` (no matching feature, so
      project-wide is the default — explicitly chosen over surfacing
      an irrelevant scope).
    - ``bug-predict`` workflow → first non-glob ``files`` entry of
      the ``bug-predict`` feature, if any.

    Returns ``""`` when ``features.yaml`` is missing, when there's no
    matching feature, or when the matching feature has ``path=None``
    (e.g. its ``files`` are all mid-name globs).
    """
    for feature in list_features(project_root):
        if feature.name == workflow_name and feature.path:
            return feature.path
    return ""


def derive_project_name(project_root: Path | str) -> str:
    """Return a human-readable project name for the dashboard header.

    Reads the ``[project]`` table's ``name`` field from
    ``<project_root>/pyproject.toml`` when present; falls back to the
    directory basename otherwise. The fallback gives sensible output
    for projects without a ``pyproject.toml`` (Node.js, plain
    directories) while the pyproject path means worktree-launched
    dashboards display the package name (e.g. ``attune-ai``) instead
    of the worktree slug (e.g. ``reverent-brown-937823``).

    Defensive failure modes — none of these surface to the user; the
    dashboard just renders the basename:

    - Missing ``pyproject.toml`` → basename.
    - Unreadable file (perm error, OSError) → basename.
    - Malformed TOML → basename.
    - ``[project]`` table missing or ``name`` field missing → basename.
    - Empty ``name`` value → basename (don't render blank header).

    No-pyproject fallback chain isn't extended to ancestor
    directories: the dashboard's ``--project-root`` is supposed to
    BE the project root. Walking up could surface a parent
    workspace's name (e.g. ``Users``) which is worse than the
    worktree slug.
    """
    root = Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve()
    pyproject = root / "pyproject.toml"
    if pyproject.is_file():
        try:
            text = pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except OSError:
            return root.name
        # Python 3.11+ ships tomllib; fall back to the stdlib parser.
        try:
            import tomllib
        except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover — Python < 3.11
            try:
                import tomli as tomllib  # type: ignore[no-redef]
            except ImportError:
                return root.name
        try:
            parsed = tomllib.loads(text)
        except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
            return root.name
        project_table = parsed.get("project")
        if isinstance(project_table, dict):
            name = project_table.get("name")
            if isinstance(name, str) and name.strip():
                return name.strip()
    return root.name


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Session:
    """One Claude Code session — what surfaces on the dashboard's /sessions page.

    Built from a JSONL file in
    ``~/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-root>/<session-id>.jsonl``.
    The JSONL is an event log of queue operations + attachments; we
    care about events with a ``content`` field (the user's prompts)
    for heuristic starter-prompt generation.

    ``source`` is ``"heuristic"`` for S2 (this slice's only path).
    S3 will introduce ``"haiku"`` and ``"cached"`` for LLM-summarized
    prompts and cache hits respectively. Surfacing the source in the
    JSON contract from day 1 means the UI can show a badge later
    without a model-field migration.
    """

    id: str
    started_at: str
    last_activity: str
    duration_seconds: float
    message_count: int
    starter_prompt: str
    source: str = "heuristic"


def _encoded_project_path(project_root: Path | str) -> str:
    """Claude Code encodes its project subdir as ``path.replace('/', '-')``.

    Resolves to absolute first so a relative ``project_root`` arg
    still matches the on-disk encoding. Returns the encoded
    basename only — the caller prepends ``~/.claude/projects/``.

    Three characters are mapped to ``-`` so the resulting string is
    safe to concatenate as a single path segment on every platform:

    - ``/`` — POSIX path separator (matches Claude Code's documented
      encoding).
    - ``\\`` — Windows path separator. ``Path.resolve()`` produces
      backslashes on Windows.
    - ``:`` — Windows drive-letter delimiter (``D:``). Without
      this, the encoded string contains a literal ``D:`` prefix that
      pathlib treats as a drive specifier on subsequent
      ``Path / encoded`` concatenation, silently discarding the
      ``~/.claude/projects/`` prefix and rooting the result at the
      bogus drive.

    POSIX paths never contain backslash or colon, so the two
    Windows-only replacements are no-ops there.
    """
    resolved = str(Path(project_root).expanduser().resolve())
    return resolved.replace("/", "-").replace("\\", "-").replace(":", "-")


def claude_sessions_dir(project_root: Path | str) -> Path:
    """Return the directory Claude Code stores sessions for this project in.

    Doesn't check existence — callers should treat a non-existent
    dir as "no sessions yet" rather than an error condition (the
    dir is created on first session, which the user may not have
    started in this project).
    """
    return Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects" / _encoded_project_path(project_root)


def _heuristic_starter_prompt(content: str, *, char_limit: int = 200) -> str:
    """Truncate a user's first-prompt content to ~``char_limit`` chars.

    Spec calls for first user prompt + last assistant turn, both
    truncated. The Claude Code JSONL we observed only carries the
    user-prompt side via queue-operation enqueue events; there's no
    assistant-turn signal in this event log. S2 ships with the
    user-prompt-only heuristic; S3's Haiku path produces the
    fuller summary independently of this code path.

    Truncation strategy: cut at a word boundary if one falls within
    ``char_limit - 20`` of the limit so we don't slice mid-word.
    Ellipsis appended when truncated.
    """
    s = (content or "").strip().replace("\n", " ")
    # Collapse runs of whitespace so the preview doesn't have gaps.
    s = " ".join(s.split())
    if len(s) <= char_limit:
        return s
    cut = s[:char_limit]
    last_space = cut.rfind(" ")
    if last_space > char_limit - 20:
        cut = cut[:last_space]
    return cut.rstrip() + "…"


def _parse_session(jsonl_path: Path) -> Session | None:
    """Build a :class:`Session` from one JSONL file. Returns None on
    unreadable file (callers skip rather than crash the listing).

    Robust per-line: a malformed JSON line is skipped, not fatal.
    A file with zero parseable lines yields a Session with empty
    timestamps and a "(empty session)" starter prompt — the
    template can render the row OR the caller can filter; we
    surface rather than hide.
    """
    session_id = jsonl_path.stem
    first_ts: str | None = None
    last_ts: str | None = None
    prompt_count = 0
    starter_prompt = ""
    try:
        with jsonl_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for raw in fh:
                line = raw.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    event = json.loads(line)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue
                if not isinstance(event, dict):
                    continue
                ts = event.get("timestamp")
                if isinstance(ts, str) and ts:
                    if first_ts is None:
                        first_ts = ts
                    last_ts = ts
                content = event.get("content")
                if isinstance(content, str) and content:
                    prompt_count += 1
                    if not starter_prompt:
                        starter_prompt = _heuristic_starter_prompt(content)
    except OSError:
        return None
    duration = _duration_seconds(first_ts, last_ts)
    return Session(
        id=session_id,
        started_at=first_ts or "",
        last_activity=last_ts or first_ts or "",
        duration_seconds=duration,
        message_count=prompt_count,
        starter_prompt=starter_prompt or "(no prompt recorded)",
        source="heuristic",
    )


def _duration_seconds(first: str | None, last: str | None) -> float:
    """ISO 8601 strings → elapsed seconds; ``0.0`` if either is unparseable."""
    if not first or not last:
        return 0.0
    try:
        a = datetime.fromisoformat(first.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        b = datetime.fromisoformat(last.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0
    return max((b - a).total_seconds(), 0.0)


def list_recent_sessions(
    project_root: Path | str,
    *,
    days: int = 3,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> list[Session]:
    """Return Session records for this project's last ``days`` of activity.

    Reads ``~/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-root>/*.jsonl`` and
    filters to files whose mtime is within ``days`` of ``now``
    (default: current UTC time). Sorts most-recently-active first.

    Returns ``[]`` for any failure mode that doesn't raise:
    - Sessions dir doesn't exist (user never ran Claude Code here)
    - Sessions dir exists but is empty
    - All JSONLs are older than the cutoff
    - All JSONLs are unreadable (perm, IO)

    A single corrupt file is skipped with a WARN log; the rest of
    the listing still renders. The spec's failure-mode decision:
    "Skip with WARN log, don't surface as broken row — an unreadable
    file is a Claude Code internal issue, not something the user
    can fix from the dashboard."
    """
    # Local import: a module-level ``timedelta`` import was reverted by
    # the formatter (likely ruff isort considering it unused at the
    # module scope since only this function references it). Re-importing
    # locally is the pragmatic dodge — the cost is negligible because
    # ``from datetime import ...`` is cached after first use anyway.
    from datetime import timedelta

    sessions_dir = claude_sessions_dir(project_root)
    if not sessions_dir.is_dir():
        return []
    if now is None:
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    cutoff = now - timedelta(days=days)
    out: list[Session] = []
    try:
        candidates = list(sessions_dir.glob("*.jsonl"))
    except OSError:
        return []
    for jsonl in candidates:
        try:
            mtime = datetime.fromtimestamp(jsonl.stat().st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc)
        except OSError:
            continue
        if mtime < cutoff:
            continue
        session = _parse_session(jsonl)
        if session is None:
            continue
        out.append(session)
    out.sort(key=lambda s: s.last_activity or "", reverse=True)
    return out


# Path passed to workflows when the user picks the "All code" picker
# option. Hardcoded for attune-ai's ``src/`` layout. Downstream projects
# with different code roots can override by editing this constant or by
# threading a config value through the dashboard route — kept simple
# for the v1 ship.
ALL_CODE_PATH = "src/"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FamilyVersion:
    package: str
    version: str | None
    source: str  # "installed" | "missing"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DailyCost:
    """One day's cost for the home-page sparkline."""

    day: str  # YYYY-MM-DD
    events: int
    cost: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HomeKpis:
    """Summary numbers shown above the fold on the home page."""

    today_events: int
    today_cost: float
    seven_day_cost: float
    seven_day_savings: float
    sparkline: list[DailyCost]  # always exactly 7 entries, oldest first


def home_kpis(summary: TelemetrySummary, *, today: date | None = None) -> HomeKpis:
    """Derive home-page KPIs from a telemetry summary.

    Always returns a 7-entry sparkline (zero-fills missing days) so the SVG
    layout is stable even on a fresh install.
    """
    today = today or date.today()
    by_day_lookup = {row[0]: (row[1], row[2]) for row in summary.by_day}

    sparkline: list[DailyCost] = []
    seven_day_cost = 0.0
    for offset in range(6, -1, -1):
        day = date.fromordinal(today.toordinal() - offset).isoformat()
        events, cost = by_day_lookup.get(day, (0, 0.0))
        seven_day_cost += cost
        sparkline.append(DailyCost(day=day, events=events, cost=cost))

    today_events, today_cost = by_day_lookup.get(today.isoformat(), (0, 0.0))
    return HomeKpis(
        today_events=today_events,
        today_cost=round(today_cost, 4),
        seven_day_cost=round(seven_day_cost, 4),
        seven_day_savings=round(summary.total_savings, 4),
        sparkline=sparkline,
    )


def sparkline_points(values: list[float], *, width: int = 240, height: int = 40) -> str:
    """Render values as an SVG ``polyline`` ``points`` string.

    Empty/all-zero values return an empty string (template renders fallback).
    Y-axis is inverted (SVG origin is top-left); the largest value touches
    the top of the box.
    """
    if not values or all(v == 0 for v in values):
        return ""
    n = len(values)
    span = max(values) or 1.0
    points: list[str] = []
    for i, v in enumerate(values):
        x = (i / max(n - 1, 1)) * width
        y = height - (v / span) * height
        points.append(f"{x:.1f},{y:.1f}")
    return " ".join(points)


def read_telemetry_summary(config: Config, *, recent_days: int = 7) -> TelemetrySummary:
    """Aggregate ``usage.jsonl`` into a UI-friendly summary."""
    path = config.telemetry_path
    if not path.exists():
        return TelemetrySummary(0, 0.0, 0.0, [], [], None)

    total_requests = 0
    total_cost = 0.0
    total_savings = 0.0
    by_workflow_count: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    by_workflow_cost: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    by_day_count: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    by_day_cost: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    last_event_at: str | None = None

    try:
        with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    event: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(line)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue

                cost = float(event.get("total_cost", event.get("cost", 0.0)) or 0.0)
                savings = float(event.get("savings", 0.0) or 0.0)
                workflow = str(event.get("workflow") or event.get("event_type") or "unknown")
                # ``usage.jsonl`` events use the ``ts`` key (v1.0 schema in
                # UsageTracker._format_entry); ``timestamp`` is kept as a
                # legacy fallback for any rotated archives that predate the
                # rename. Without this fallback every event silently misses
                # the by_day bucketing and Home's KPI tiles read zero.
                ts = str(event.get("ts") or event.get("timestamp") or "")

                total_requests += 1
                total_cost += cost
                total_savings += savings
                by_workflow_count[workflow] += 1
                by_workflow_cost[workflow] += cost

                day = _to_day(ts)
                if day:
                    by_day_count[day] += 1
                    by_day_cost[day] += cost
                if ts:
                    last_event_at = ts
    except OSError:
        return TelemetrySummary(0, 0.0, 0.0, [], [], None)

    # Filter test fixtures, demo stubs, and removed workflows from the
    # top-list. The telemetry file accumulates entries from every
    # workflow that ever ran, so old test fixtures (e.g. those listed
    # in .claude/rules/attune/bug-patterns.md sync logs:
    # "test-tier-fallback", "new-sample-workflow1") pollute the top
    # spenders rollup and distort the "where did my money go?" signal.
    # The current registry is the source of truth — anything not in it
    # is either a removed workflow or a stub from local development.
    # (P2-8 in the 2026-05-14 QA punch list.)
    try:
        canonical_names = {w.name for w in list_workflows()}
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        # INTENTIONAL: if the registry introspection fails, fall back
        # to showing everything rather than hiding all data.
        canonical_names = None

    def _is_canonical(name: str) -> bool:
        if canonical_names is None:
            return True
        return name in canonical_names

    filtered = [
        (k, by_workflow_count[k], round(by_workflow_cost[k], 4))
        for k in by_workflow_count
        if _is_canonical(k)
    ]
    by_workflow = sorted(filtered, key=lambda row: row[2], reverse=True)[:20]

    today = date.today()
    cutoff = today.toordinal() - recent_days
    recent_days_data = sorted(
        (
            (day, by_day_count[day], round(by_day_cost[day], 4))
            for day in by_day_count
            if _ordinal(day) is not None and _ordinal(day) >= cutoff
        ),
        key=lambda row: row[0],
    )

    return TelemetrySummary(
        total_requests=total_requests,
        total_cost=round(total_cost, 4),
        total_savings=round(total_savings, 4),
        by_workflow=by_workflow,
        by_day=recent_days_data,
        last_event_at=last_event_at,
    )


def list_workflows() -> list[WorkflowEntry]:
    """Return the registered workflow catalog. Empty if the registry is unavailable."""
    try:
        from attune.workflows import list_workflows as registry_list
    except ImportError:
        return []

    out: list[WorkflowEntry] = []
    try:
        for entry in registry_list():
            stages = entry.get("stages") or []
            tier_map = entry.get("tier_map") or {}
            out.append(
                WorkflowEntry(
                    name=str(entry.get("name", "")),
                    description=str(entry.get("description", "")),
                    stages=len(stages) if isinstance(stages, list) else 0,
                    tier_map={str(k): str(v) for k, v in tier_map.items()},
                )
            )
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        # INTENTIONAL: registry introspection is best-effort; never fail the dashboard.
        return []
    return sorted(out, key=lambda w: w.name)


def family_versions() -> list[FamilyVersion]:
    """Resolve installed versions for every related attune package."""
    packages = ("attune-ai", "attune-author", "attune-rag", "attune-help", "attune-gui")
    return [_resolve_version(pkg) for pkg in packages]


def env_health(config: Config) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Lightweight environment snapshot for the Health page."""
    import platform
    import sys as _sys

    home = config.attune_home
    return {
        "python": _sys.version.split()[0],
        "platform": platform.platform(),
        "attune_home": str(home),
        "attune_home_exists": home.exists(),
        "telemetry_present": config.telemetry_path.exists(),
        "memory_dir_present": config.memory_dir.exists(),
        "sessions_dir_present": config.sessions_dir.exists(),
        "project_root": str(config.project_root),
        "anthropic_api_key": bool(_env("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")),
    }


def _to_day(ts: str) -> str | None:
    if not ts:
        return None
    with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
        # Tolerate trailing Z, naive, or aware ISO timestamps.
        cleaned = ts.rstrip("Z")
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(cleaned)
        if dt.tzinfo is None:
            dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        return dt.date().isoformat()
    return None


def _ordinal(day: str) -> int | None:
    with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
        return date.fromisoformat(day).toordinal()
    return None


def _env(name: str) -> str | None:
    import os

    return os.environ.get(name)


def _resolve_version(package: str) -> FamilyVersion:
    try:
        from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError
        from importlib.metadata import version as _version
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover — Python <3.10 not supported
        return FamilyVersion(package=package, version=None, source="missing")
    try:
        return FamilyVersion(package=package, version=_version(package), source="installed")
    except PackageNotFoundError:
        return FamilyVersion(package=package, version=None, source="missing")
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        # INTENTIONAL: metadata resolution is best-effort.
        return FamilyVersion(package=package, version=None, source="missing")

1	"""Redaction pass for Claude Code session content before LLM summarization.
2	
3	Defined by the ops-sessions-page spec (decisions.md, Decision 3).
4	Runs over the user's first prompts or any text destined for Haiku
5	summarization. The redacted text is what gets sent to the model AND
6	what gets cached on disk — sensitive material never lands in either
7	the LLM provider's context or our `<attune_home>/ops/session_summaries/`
8	cache.
9	
10	The patterns target the realistic threat surface for a developer's
11	session content: API keys committed to scratch buffers, paths
12	revealing the user's filesystem layout, IPs, and email addresses
13	the user didn't authorize as identifying themselves.
14	
15	Discipline: redact FIRST, then summarize, then cache. Cache hits
16	return the redacted form — no re-redaction needed on read.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import ipaddress
22	import re
23	from collections.abc import Iterable
24	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
25	
26	# Default redaction placeholder. A short, identifiable token so a
27	# human reading a summary knows the model saw a redacted region.
28	_PLACEHOLDER = "<redacted>"
29	_PLACEHOLDER_HOME = "<user-home>"
30	_PLACEHOLDER_EMAIL = "<redacted-email>"
31	_PLACEHOLDER_IP = "<redacted-ip>"
32	
33	# Email allowlist — these can appear in summaries without redaction.
34	# Sourced from CLAUDE.md user profile. Edit when the team / owner
35	# set expands.
36	_EMAIL_ALLOWLIST: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
37	    {
38	        "silversurfer562@gmail.com",
39	        "admin@smartaimemory.com",
40	        "patrick.roebuck@smartaimemory.com",
41	    }
42	)
43	
44	
45	# Concrete API-key shapes. Each pattern is anchored to avoid eating
46	# adjacent non-key text. The order matters: more specific patterns
47	# first so generic fallbacks don't consume them.
48	_API_KEY_PATTERNS: tuple[re.Pattern[str], ...] = (
49	    # Anthropic
50	    re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}"),
51	    # Generic OpenAI-style
52	    re.compile(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"),
53	    # GitHub PATs (pre-2021 hex format intentionally NOT listed —
54	    # too generic). Modern prefixed tokens:
55	    re.compile(r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}"),
56	    re.compile(r"gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}"),
57	    re.compile(r"ghu_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}"),
58	    re.compile(r"ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}"),
59	    re.compile(r"ghr_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}"),
60	    # Slack bot tokens
61	    re.compile(r"xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9\-]{10,}"),
62	    # AWS access keys
63	    re.compile(r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"),
64	    # Bearer-style auth headers
65	    re.compile(r"Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-+/=]{20,}"),
66	)
67	
68	# Generic high-entropy token preceded by a key/secret-context word
69	# within ~5 characters of an assignment operator. Matches an
70	# assignment of a credential-named identifier to a 16+-char quoted
71	# value. Keywords matched: password, passwd, pwd, secret, token,
72	# api_key / api-key, access_key / access-key, auth.
73	#
74	# Concrete example strings are intentionally omitted from this
75	# comment. The project's hardcoded-secrets scanner test
76	# (tests/unit/security/test_security_remediation.py) flags any
77	# credential-keyword + equals + quoted-string sequence in src/
78	# regardless of surrounding context.
79	#
80	# Anchored so prose like "the credential parameter is required"
81	# does not false-fire. The value character class includes common
82	# password punctuation (``!@#$%^&*~``) so a real-world password
83	# value still matches even when it isn't a pure-base64 token.
84	_CONTEXT_KEY_PATTERN = re.compile(
85	    r"\b(?:password|passwd|pwd|secret|token|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|auth)"
86	    r"\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Za-z0-9._\-+/=!@#$%^&*~]{16,})['\"]?",
87	    flags=re.IGNORECASE,
88	)
89	
90	# Absolute path under a user-home directory.
91	#   /Users/<name>/...   (macOS)
92	#   /home/<name>/...    (Linux)
93	#   C:\Users\<name>\... (Windows, backslash form)
94	#   C:/Users/<name>/... (Windows, forward-slash form some shells use)
95	_USER_HOME_PATTERNS: tuple[re.Pattern[str], ...] = (
96	    re.compile(r"/Users/[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+(?=/|$|\s|['\"])"),
97	    re.compile(r"/home/[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+(?=/|$|\s|['\"])"),
98	    re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]:[\\\/]Users[\\\/][A-Za-z0-9._\-]+(?=[\\\/]|$|\s|['\"])"),
99	)
100	
101	# Email address — RFC 5322 simplified. Matched, then checked against
102	# the allowlist before redacting.
103	_EMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(
104	    r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b",
105	)
106	
107	# IP addresses — match candidate, validate with ipaddress.ip_address.
108	# Conservative: only redact RFC1918 private + obvious public IPv4. IPv6
109	# matching deferred (rarely in user prompts; can extend later).
110	_IPV4_CANDIDATE = re.compile(r"\b(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}\b")
111	
112	
113	@dataclass(frozen=True)
114	class RedactionResult:
115	    """Outcome of a redaction pass.
116	
117	    ``text`` is the redacted output. ``counts`` is a per-category
118	    histogram useful for logging and for fixture-construction
119	    confidence ("did we actually redact anything in this session?").
120	    Counts are diagnostic, not security-critical — code paths that
121	    branch on whether redaction occurred should use ``text != input``
122	    instead, since a category may have counted overlapping matches.
123	    """
124	
125	    text: str
126	    counts: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
127	
128	
129	def redact(
130	    text: str,
131	    *,
132	    email_allowlist: Iterable[str] | None = None,
133	) -> RedactionResult:
134	    """Run all redaction passes over ``text`` and return the result.
135	
136	    Order of operations is deliberate — patterns higher on the list
137	    take precedence so a string like ``sk-ant-xxx`` is caught by the
138	    specific Anthropic pattern before the generic context-key pattern
139	    sees it.
140	
141	    Args:
142	        text: The input string. Typically a user's first prompt from
143	            a Claude Code session JSONL.
144	        email_allowlist: Override for the default email allowlist.
145	            Pass an explicit set to swap the policy at call time (e.g.
146	            stricter set in shared-machine contexts). When ``None``,
147	            the module-level default is used.
148	
149	    Returns:
150	        A :class:`RedactionResult` with the redacted ``text`` and a
151	        per-category ``counts`` histogram.
152	    """
153	    if not text:
154	        return RedactionResult(text=text or "", counts={})
155	
156	    allowlist = (
157	        frozenset(s.lower() for s in email_allowlist)
158	        if email_allowlist is not None
159	        else _EMAIL_ALLOWLIST
160	    )
161	
162	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
163	    out = text
164	
165	    # 1. API-key shapes (highest specificity first).
166	    for pattern in _API_KEY_PATTERNS:
167	        out, n = pattern.subn(_PLACEHOLDER, out)
168	        if n:
169	            counts["api_key"] = counts.get("api_key", 0) + n
170	
171	    # 2. Context-key fallback for anything resembling a credential
172	    # assignment that the specific patterns didn't catch.
173	    def _ck_sub(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
174	        # Replace only the value portion, preserve the key + operator
175	        # so a human reader of the summary sees what was redacted.
176	        full = match.group(0)
177	        value = match.group(1)
178	        return full.replace(value, _PLACEHOLDER, 1)
179	
180	    out, n = _CONTEXT_KEY_PATTERN.subn(_ck_sub, out)
181	    if n:
182	        counts["context_key"] = n
183	
184	    # 3. User-home absolute paths.
185	    for pattern in _USER_HOME_PATTERNS:
